notes: Source 4 = Biran 1985, Eretz-Israel 18, section B (Hebrew); quotes are from the packet's English translation. s4f1 is the only feature described first-hand. It lies on the hilltop (Area A) 'north of Locus 103' beside the western enclosure wall W2 (Pl. 40:2), so its direction is from a locus (relative_to other), not from the site. Hellenistic and Roman sherds came from the cleaning of the blocked channel. s4f2-s4f4 rest on the article's quotations of Press and of the Staff Officer's survey (cisterns, caves, 'a tomb'); s4f3 also on the author's own site description. None has a position or date; the tomb's type is not given. Not coded: the plaster layer on bedrock in the pillared building (L. 202), the kiln, and the unlabelled dashed circle L.204 on Fig. 3 (no text). No plan position: Figs. 2-3 have no coordinates, so the unit's recorded point cannot be placed.
